actions: externally rotates hip (in extension); abducts hip (in flexion, due to its line of pull crossing above the hip center)

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population

neuromuscular_junction_zone.location_description: mid-belly endplate band -- for where this band lies along the muscle, see motor_endplate_zones

functional_compartments.function_note: Passes through the greater sciatic foramen, dividing it into supra- and infra-piriform spaces -- the sciatic nerve's relationship to this muscle (usually passing below it, but a documented anatomical variant splits or passes through it) is the anatomical basis of piriformis syndrome.
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

motor_endplate_zones.notes: Given in the source as between three-fifths and four-fifths of the distance along the muscle. The sciatic nerve lies close to this target, which is the stated reason ultrasound guidance is used here.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part III -- Proximal Lower Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(5):240 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17050240 -- review synthesis of the intramuscular neural arborization literature it cites

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transverse on the posterior surface of the hip joint, angled about 20 degrees laterally toward the sacrum, roughly 8 cm lateral to the sacrum and 10 cm proximal to the ischial tuberosity.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Deep to gluteus maximus, lying on the acetabular cortex.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: From deep to superficial the sequence is acetabular cortex, piriformis, then gluteus maximus.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Injected both for spasm and for the pain of piriformis syndrome, where the muscle compresses the sciatic nerve -- so the structure at risk is also the reason for treating.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part III -- Proximal Lower Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(5):240 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17050240 -- review synthesis of the intramuscular neural arborization literature it cites
